svg.aria-label: A one-page design for Kettle Hollow: the whole valley as a map, with a gameplay-minutes ruler along the bottom aligning six landmarks to the first twenty-four minutes of play.
svg.title: Kettle Hollow, time and space
svg.desc: Map plus timeline archetype. Six landmarks, the route through them, difficulty zones, and a minutes ruler so pacing and layout can be read against each other.

g.inkscape:label: 10 Title
g.text: The whole valley, and the first 24 minutes of play, on one sheet.

g.inkscape:label: 45 Routes
g.text: ridge shortcut, opens only after the cave

g.inkscape:label: 50 Callouts
g.text: The Split needs hover. CharacterController has
no hover field and script cannot reach velocity.
Swim is taught here because drowning is impossible:
the shallows have no deep water and no current.

g.inkscape:label: 55 Sidebar
g.text: Walk, swim, climb. Nothing can kill you.
The yard, then the gap. First real failure.
The cave is dark and unguided. The ridge
Every one is on the Creative Mode rail, so
the whole valley is authorable without script.
Landmark 4 is the only place in the valley
that cannot be built today. Everything else
Until G1 closes, The Split is a water
crossing and the timeline is unchanged.

g.inkscape:label: 60 Timeline
g.text: The ruler is the point of this sheet. Landmark 4 sits at minute 11, one third of the way in, which is where the first real failure belongs.
Move it earlier and the player has not been taught enough to read it as fair. Later, and the middle of the valley has no teeth.
product/design/diagrams/onepager-kettle-hollow-timeline.svg · original content · minutes are intent, not measurement
